releaseNotes: Expanded onboarding into typed ONB-00 through ONB-22 catalog nodes so the durable engine can schedule, fan out, join, checkpoint, retry, resume, and verify the complete consumer onboarding system rather than executing one coarse prose node.

Rebuilt product/ONBOARDING.md as the canonical evidence, first-value, state, identity, analytics, design, monetization, lifecycle, implementation, hard-cutover, and zero-legacy contract, with a faithful searchable generated HTML view.

Added check:onboarding-graph to both package layouts and the standard audit, with deterministic fixtures for review timing, deferrals, placeholder completion, typed screen and control contracts, and legacy removal. Updated app-agent roles to continue the graph through Compound Engineering implementation and final proof.

CI review pass: fixed a ReferenceError in check-onboarding-graph.ts where TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS was declared after tablePlaceholderCells() could already be called from top-level script code (moved the const above its first use), applied Prettier formatting, and added the missing docs/plans/attachments/2026-08-port-ledger.md row (plus rebased onto origin/main, which had advanced with unrelated merges since this branch was cut).

Fixed three interlocking bugs in tablePlaceholderCells() that a full local audit run surfaced once the TDZ crash above stopped masking them. 'done' was in the bare generic-completion-word blocklist, so the Graph Run table's own correct terminal status value made check:onboarding-graph reject every real completed onboarding lane -- removed it (graphRunNodeDone() already requires it literally, so it needs no separate placeholder check). The repeated-cell heuristic keyed on first-word-only, so a genuinely filled Evidence Ledger with many distinct 'Evidence-N: ...' rows tripped it purely because they share a label prefix -- switched to whole-cell-text repetition, which still catches an actually-unfilled table (identical text repeated) without false-positiving on distinct content. onboarding.fixtures.ts's own fillTemplateDirectiveCells() only replaced cells starting with literally 'Record', leaving the shipped template's other directive-verb cells ('Define', 'Choose', etc.) unfilled, so its 'completed' fixture was never actually complete -- broadened it to mirror the validator's own TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS set (then hit and fixed the identical before-first-use TDZ ordering bug in that same fixture file). Also corrected the port ledger's grand-total row: my own counting script had matched the summary table's own header row as if it were a data row, overstating every bucket by one.

Closed the review round on the full onboarding graph: ONB-22's catalog gate now runs check-onboarding-graph.ts --require-done, a new wrapper that rejects the shipped template (lane still not_started) while leaving the general audit's lenient check:onboarding-graph untouched -- registered the wrapper as a deliberate audit-plan exclusion so catalog validation and package-parity both accept it, and added fixtures proving both the reject and a genuinely-completed accept. ONB-18 now depends on the real Design Room workflow instead of only narrating a high-fidelity prototype in its own Markdown packet, so the engine cannot unblock ONB-20 on prose alone. Re-verified against ground truth (not assumption) that the regex, catalog-encoding, Copy-column, deferred-lane, and placeholder-detection review threads were already fixed by earlier commits on this branch, and re-ran the full launchbench and catalog fixture suites to confirm. Aligned the review-prompt timing doctrine (earn eligibility at first value, request later outside first-run onboarding) across emotional-design-system.md, consumer-product-design-agency.md, influencer-sponsorship-engine.md, and launchbench-evals.md's own failure-mode index, which still described the pre-onboarding-conversion.md timing after push-notification-lifecycle.md was already fixed.

A second review round found six more real gaps behind --require-done's own logic, not just doctrine drift. ONB-22 was classified actionClass 'mutate', letting the durable engine execute its hard cutover and legacy deletion under an ordinary experience-domain grant instead of the autonomy engine's protected destructive waiver path -- reclassified it 'destructive' with a founderOnlyActions entry. The not_needed/deferred skip exempted --require-done too, so a deferred workspace passed ONB-22's own strict gate without ever finishing onboarding -- the skip now applies only to the general (non-strict) invocation. The strict block checked every ONB node's Graph Run table entry and every table cell's placeholder state but never the Verification section's own '- [ ] ...' checklist, so a fixture leaving all eleven final checks unchecked still passed --require-done -- added a dedicated unchecked-item count. graphRunNodeDone() searched every cell in a Graph Run row for the literal word 'done' instead of reading the Status column specifically, so a 'partial' row mentioning 'done' in its owner or result prose was wrongly accepted -- it now locates the Status column by the table's own header before reading it. tablePlaceholderCells()'s generic completion-word blocklist rejected legitimate prescribed terminal answers ('Yes', 'Pass', 'N/A', ...) that the template itself asks for in the Effort-Before-Value, policy, and Prototype And Design Proof matrices -- removed the blocklist, keeping only the literal word 'placeholder', the directive-verb first-word check, and the whole-cell repetition heuristic. And product/onboarding.html's decoded raw-source view carried internal vocabulary (lane, gate, artifact, not_started, ...) into the browser-visible DOM behind a static <script>/<pre> pair that check-founder-copy.ts's script-stripping scan could never see regardless of surrounding markup -- moved the source view into the repo's sanctioned <details>'Technical details' disclosure (the same pattern render-launch-cockpit.ts and render-design-room.ts already use) and taught check-founder-copy.ts to decode base64 script payloads and scan them too, exempting only the ones whose target element actually sits inside that disclosure. Verified the founder-copy fix by reverting the HTML locally and confirming the gate now genuinely fails the leak, not just structurally happens to pass.

A third review round found the remaining table-only blind spot: tablePlaceholderCells() and graphRunNodeDone() only ever looked at table rows, so the Execution Mode section's own directive-verb-led paragraph ('Record `greenfield`, ...') and seven similar prose sections stayed exactly as the shipped template wrote them under --require-done, and the artifact's own top-of-document 'Status: `word`' header was never cross-checked against the done lane it was claiming. Added proseDirectiveLines() (same TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS first-word check as the table version, folded into the existing onboarding_graph.placeholder_complete error) and a dedicated onboarding_graph.artifact_status_not_done check requiring the header to read exactly done. The fixture-side prose filler swaps only each directive line's leading verb for a word outside TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS_PATTERN rather than replacing the whole line, because several of these same sentences (e.g. the First Value And Activation paragraph) are also where requirePhrases() finds its required doctrine phrases -- a whole-line replacement would have silently broken those checks instead of fixing this one.

A fourth review round found the placeholder-detection heuristics were still gameable rather than content-checking. tablePlaceholderCells()'s whole-cell repetition check missed boilerplate that varies only by an embedded counter (e.g. 'Evidence-1: source-backed implementation detail dated 2026-08-08', 'Evidence-2: ...'), which is exactly the shape of the fixture's own former filler and, per a direct count against the shipped template, would also have let a real launch fill 84 of 138 directive cells with a single copy-pasted sentence -- added a digit-normalized repetition count (digits collapsed to '#') alongside the exact-text one, so counter-varying filler is caught without rejecting genuinely distinct rows. proseDirectiveLines() was, in the same round, found to over-flag: two fixed doctrine sentences (Analytics Contract's 'Define a machine-readable schema...' and First Value And Activation's 'Define First value rendered...') sit directly above their own capture table and carry required doctrine phrases verbatim, so a genuinely complete artifact that correctly left them untouched would have failed -- scoped the check to only flag a directive-verb-led line when its own section (down to the next heading) has no table. And the not_needed/deferred skip accepted a bare status with no explanation, since check-lane-coverage.ts already treats nonempty evidence as sufficient rationale for a skip even though evidence answers 'did the lane produce anything' rather than 'why is it not happening' -- added onboarding_graph.deferred_without_reason, requiring a recorded blocker or reason before the exemption applies. Rewrote the fixture's own fillTemplateDirectiveCells() to derive each filled cell's text from its own row's identifying content and column header instead of an incrementing counter, so the 'genuinely completed' fixture states remain immune to the new normalized-repetition check while staying a faithful test of real validator behavior; added dedicated fixtures proving the counter-boilerplate rejection, the fixed-doctrine-prose exemption, and the deferred-without-reason rejection.

A fifth review round found two engine-wiring defects rather than validator logic gaps. runDeterministicGates() (core/session/run.ts) invokes every gate via `npm run --prefix <skillRoot> <gate>`, and npm's own documented --prefix behavior executes the underlying script with the package root as process.cwd() regardless of the caller's actual working directory -- confirmed empirically with a standalone reproduction. The engine already set BUSINESS_ROOT in the child's env for exactly this reason, but parseCliArgs() (tooling/lib/launch-state.ts, shared by 43+ business validators) never read it, defaulting root to process.cwd() unconditionally -- so ONB-22's gate, and every other durable-engine-invoked deterministic gate, resolved the skill package instead of the business workspace and could never pass even on a genuinely completed launch. Fixed by defaulting root to BUSINESS_ROOT when set, before an explicit --root flag (still checked afterward) can override it for direct CLI use; verified by reproducing the exact npm run --prefix invocation with and without BUSINESS_ROOT, confirming it now correctly resolves the workspace. Separately, ONB-03 through ONB-08 -- the six research nodes evidence-joined by ONB-09 -- were domain.experience with no gate command, which compilePlan() compiles to verification 'none': an empty or fabricated research packet could unlock ONB-09 and the later destructive cutover with no check at all. Reassigned all six to domain.research, matching the existing workflow.research.* convention (domainId drives compilePlan()'s JUDGMENT_DOMAINS fresh-context routing; areaIds stays area.product-experience), so each now requires fresh-context judgment verification before being accepted.

A sixth review round found the round-5 domain.research reassignment itself was wrong in production: core/session/run.ts's acceptVerification() -- the only thing that can promote a reconciled-but-blocked node to succeeded -- is called from exactly one site, inside the deterministic-gate branch; fresh_context acceptance has no production caller anywhere, only test fixtures (verification/fixtures/engine.fixtures.ts), so ONB-03 through ONB-08 would have stayed permanently blocked in a real run, and the domain reassignment also silently dropped them out of an experience-scoped session brief's dispatch scope (scopeHints: ['domain.experience']). Reverted all six nodes to domain.experience and instead gave each an explicit deterministic gate (check:onboarding-evidence-onb-03 through -08, added to both package.json layouts, registered as deliberate audit-plan and launchbench exclusions since each checks a specific node's own mid-run output packet that does not exist against the shipped, never-executed template) via a new validation/business/experience/check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts, which rejects a missing, stub-length (<400 non-fence characters), still-templated (TODO/TBD/PLACEHOLDER/not_started), or prose-free packet -- the same structural-only limitation as every other deterministic gate in this system, since judging whether research is actually true still has no production verifier. This is the more robust fix: deterministic gates have a working production acceptance path, so it closes the original round-5 gap (verification 'none') without reintroducing either of round 6's regressions. Caught a self-inflicted bug during fixture verification: the new fixture helper's `'text' + topic + '. '.repeat(15)` only repeated the trailing '. ', not the full sentence, so the 'passing' fixture was actually testing a 179-character stub and failed its own assertion -- fixed by building the full sentence first, then repeating it.

The same round also flagged ONB-20 (adversarial QA): domain.experience with no gate compiled to verification 'none', so an empty ONB-20-adversarial-qa.md could unlock ONB-21 and the destructive ONB-22 cutover with no policy, instrumentation, accessibility, or provider QA behind it. Fixed with the same pattern as ONB-03..08 -- gates: ['check:onboarding-evidence-onb-20'] reusing the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts validator, registered as the same audit-plan exclusion, with fixtures proving the missing- and passing-packet cases.

A seventh review round found four more real gaps. ONB-22 was idempotent: true, but detectOrphans() (core/engine/runstate.ts) hands an idempotent node's orphaned attempt straight back to 'ready' for blind re-dispatch -- safe for a retryable content mutation, not for a node that applies a one-time provider/runtime transformation and deletes legacy architecture, where a lost heartbeat could mean the destructive work partially landed already. Set idempotent: false so an orphaned ONB-22 attempt instead routes to needs_readback and waits for a provider read-back to establish ground truth. Separately, ONB-22's own gate (check:onboarding-graph-complete) reads only product/ONBOARDING.md and project state, so it could accept a run that left product/onboarding.html missing or stale; added check:generated-pages -- the existing mechanism that byte-matches every authored-from page against a fresh render of its Markdown source -- to ONB-22's gates. That surfaced a real production bug in the process: check-generated-pages.ts computed its own business-root default independently of parseCliArgs (tooling/lib/launch-state.ts) instead of reusing it, so it never read BUSINESS_ROOT, and its skill-relative fallback path did not even exist -- masked until now because run-audit.ts's rootArgs always passed an explicit --root. Fixed by honoring BUSINESS_ROOT first (matching the round-5 parseCliArgs fix) and correcting the broken fallback to point at workspace/business, the same template templatesRoot() already uses; verified all three resolution paths (BUSINESS_ROOT env, explicit --root, and the corrected default) independently. Finally, knowledge/process/artifact-contracts.md still described the pre-onboarding-conversion.md App Review popup timing ('immediately after the first value/value-reveal screen') in three places, missed from the earlier doctrine-alignment sweep -- corrected to the canonical earn-eligibility-then-request-later-outside-onboarding wording from onboarding-conversion.md:94 -- and its product/onboarding.html section claimed the page was 'the visual proof for onboarding and paywall flow' requiring mobile-dimension screens and mascot states, which conflicts with the page's actual shipped implementation (a rendered execution-record document with a collapsed source disclosure, per tooling/lib/artifact-pages.ts's renderSourceArtifactPage) -- rewrote the section to describe the page's real role and point onboarding's visual-proof requirement at design/design.html (fulfilled by the Design Room), which already carries it.

An eighth review round found three more production-correctness gaps. First, ONB-22's gate (check-onboarding-graph.ts) read lanes.onboarding only from state/PROJECT_STATE.yaml (v1), but core/session/run.ts's resolveWorkspacePaths() treats state/business-state.json (v2) as a durable-engine-managed workspace's canonical state, which may have no PROJECT_STATE.yaml at all -- so ONB-22 could report the lane permanently missing on a genuinely completed v2 run. Rather than a repo-wide v1/v2 bridge (the validator suite's other ~27 loadProjectState() callers touch v2 sections -- project, narrative, autonomy, continuity, control-plane -- with no verified 1:1 v1 shape, where a wrong silent mapping would be worse than the current clear error), added loadLaneFromBusinessStateV2() to tooling/lib/launch-state.ts, scoped to exactly the one field this gate needs, with an inverse status map that core/schema/migrate-v1.ts's migrateLaneStatus() guarantees is total for a lane's six possible values; error messages now cite whichever state file actually supplied the data. Second, ONB-21 (Compound Engineering plan) had no gate and domain.experience isn't a JUDGMENT_DOMAINS entry, so compilePlan() assigned verification 'none' and an executor could return its declared artifact ID with no real plan behind it, unblocking the destructive ONB-22 cutover -- fixed with the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern as ONB-03..08/ONB-20. Third, a domain.experience-scoped session could never dispatch the onboarding graph at all: ONB-00 depends on workflow.data.analytics-and-attribution-blueprint (domain.data), and core/session/run.ts's dispatch loop only ever filtered the CURRENT ready frontier by scope, silently breaking with no explanation when scoping emptied it -- never expanding into the dependency closure to find why. Expanding the closure to auto-dispatch out-of-scope work was rejected as an authorization-boundary risk (a scoped session must never silently run work outside its founder-granted scope); instead added findOutOfScopeBlockers(), which walks only not-yet-succeeded in-scope nodes' dependency chains to name the actual blocker without touching dispatch. The first implementation flagged the wrong cases -- any out-of-scope ready node, not just an actual blocker for in-scope work -- which broke an existing fixture asserting that unrelated out-of-scope ready work is correctly left silent; corrected before shipping, and both the original and the new fixture pass. The first draft anomaly message also would have put raw domainId strings like 'domain.money' directly into a founder-facing digest, exactly what the internal-vocabulary blocklist exists to catch -- switched to citing blocked nodes by title instead.

A ninth review round found the round-8 v2-state fix itself was incomplete, plus two more real gaps. The round-8 loadLaneFromBusinessStateV2() fallback only ran when state/PROJECT_STATE.yaml was absent, but a migrated durable workspace can retain a stale v1 file alongside a live state/business-state.json -- the engine keeps updating v2 while the stale v1 value (either a permanently-blocking not_started or a falsely-authorizing done) silently wins. Fixed by checking v2 first, unconditionally, so it always takes precedence over any retained v1 file when both exist; only falls back to v1 when no v2 document exists at all. That same fallback also trusted the parsed v2 JSON's lanes.onboarding.status directly instead of validating the whole document, and the round-8 fixtures themselves used incomplete v2 objects missing required schema fields (updatedAt, project, narrative, founderGates, most lanes) that the real validator would never accept -- fixed by routing every v2 document through the repository's own validateBusinessState() schema validator and failing closed (onboarding_graph.business_state_invalid) on anything that does not fully validate, and rewrote the fixtures around a new buildValidBusinessStateV2() helper that produces a complete, schema-valid document; added a dedicated fixture proving v2 wins over a stale v1 'done' in both directions. Separately, ONB-09 (the evidence-to-decision join across ONB-03 through ONB-08) had no gate and domain.experience compiles to verification 'none', so an executor could return its declared artifact ID and fingerprint without producing a substantive join, unblocking ONB-10 through ONB-14 and ultimately ONB-22's destructive cutover with no check that the join itself ever happened -- fixed with the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern already used for ONB-03..08/ONB-20/ONB-21, with fixtures proving the missing- and passing-packet cases. Finally, graphRunNodeDone() accepted a node as done if any Graph Run table row for that node said done, without rejecting duplicate or conflicting rows -- a resumed or merged run that retains a stale row (e.g. partial) alongside a freshly appended one (e.g. done) for the same node could satisfy --require-done while the table still visibly records unfinished work. Replaced it with graphRunNodeStatus(), which requires exactly one row per node and reports onboarding_graph.node_duplicate_row when more than one exists instead of picking a side; added a fixture proving a duplicated row fails even when one copy says done.

A tenth review round found ONB-19 (implementation and cutover contract) had no gate: domain.experience with no gate compiles to verification 'none', so an executor could return its declared artifact ID and fingerprint without ever writing a substantive implementation, migration, reliability, or deletion plan, and neither ONB-20's own gate (which inspects only its own packet) nor the final graph gate (which never reads ONB-19-implementation-cutover-contract.md) would catch it -- fixed with the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern as ONB-03..08/ONB-09/ONB-20/ONB-21, with fixtures proving the missing- and passing-packet cases. Separately, and more fundamentally, ONB-22's own --require-done gate had a real deadlock: it required lanes.onboarding.status=done as its own precondition before even evaluating the artifact, but no production code path ever commits that field to done as a *result* of ONB-22's gate passing -- core/engine/runstate.ts's reconcilePatch()/acceptVerification() (the only functions the durable session runner calls on a gate pass) mutate only run-state.json and never take a business-state argument at all. Pre-setting the field beforehand does not solve this either: seedRunState() pre-accepts every node whose lane is already succeeded, including ONB-22 itself, with a fake fingerprint, so the gate would never actually run. The only two ways the field could ever become done were a one-time v1-to-v2 migration carrying over a hand-edited legacy value, or a manual out-of-band reducer commit outside the automated run loop -- neither is 'ONB-22 ran and its own check passed.' Removed the precondition; the artifact-content checks the strict block already runs unconditionally under --require-done (Graph Run table, placeholders, prose directives, Status header, Verification checklist) are the real proof of completion and are sufficient on their own -- they still reject the shipped, unstarted template exactly as before, since its Graph Run rows still read not_started. Added fixtures proving the deadlock is closed on both state generations (a v1 workspace whose lane was never marked done, and a v2 workspace whose canonical lane stays pending) once the artifact itself is genuinely complete, and reworked the v1-vs-v2 precedence fixtures that depended on the removed precondition to instead prove v2 still correctly gates whether the general (non-strict) check runs its deep validation at all.

An eleventh review round found two more ways --require-done's completion checks could be spoofed. graphRunNodeStatus() was called with the raw text instead of the fence-stripped liveText the rest of the strict block already uses, and sectionBody()'s own line search returns whichever '## Graph Run' line comes first with no regard for fences -- so an artifact that deleted its live Graph Run table and relocated an all-done copy into a fenced code sample would have that fenced sample picked up as the canonical run record, since it becomes the only '## Graph Run' heading left. Fixed by reading liveText there too. Verified by temporarily reverting the one-line fix and confirming the new fixture (which relocates the entire live Graph Run section into a fence) failed exactly as expected, then restoring the fix and confirming it passed. Separately, countUncheckedItems() only ever counted literal '- [ ]' boxes in the Verification section, so an artifact that deleted every checklist item outright -- rather than checking it off -- left an empty section that read as zero unchecked items, indistinguishable from a genuinely completed checklist. Added a minimum-item-count check (EXPECTED_VERIFICATION_ITEM_COUNT, matching the shipped template's own 11 items) alongside the existing unchecked-item check, with a new onboarding_graph.verification_items_missing error and a fixture that deletes the whole checklist and confirms it still fails even with nothing left unchecked.

A twelfth review round found the eleventh round's fence-stripping fix was too narrow, plus one more spoofable check in the sibling evidence-packet gate. liveText (the fence-stripped source) had only ever been threaded into graphRunNodeStatus(); every other structural check in check-onboarding-graph.ts -- the required-sections hasHeading() loop, the node-presence text.includes() loop, all seven requirePhrases() calls (evidence, activation, design, analytics, review, replacement, and reliability contracts), the forbidden-event-name check, and the reviewInsideFirstRun timing regex -- still ran against the raw text, so any of those required sections, node IDs, doctrine phrases, or forbidden strings could be deleted from the live document and relocated into a fenced code sample and still be found and accepted as present. Fixed by hoisting the liveText computation to the top of the artifact-processing block, before requiredSections is built, and switching every one of those checks to read it instead of text; removed the now-redundant inner liveText declaration that had only covered the --require-done block. Added a fixture that relocates the entire live 'Privacy And Security' section into a fence (the general, non---require-done check, since hasHeading() runs unconditionally) and confirms it still fails as missing. Verified by temporarily reverting hasHeading()'s call site back to raw text, confirming the new fixture failed exactly as expected, then restoring the fix and confirming the full 48-fixture onboarding suite passed. Separately, check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts's own substantive-length and prose checks stripped fenced code blocks before measuring but never HTML comments, so a <!-- ... --> block wrapping a long fake finding was invisible in the rendered packet but still counted toward the 400-character substantive-length minimum, and its first non-blank line (not starting with #, |, or -) still passed the hasProse check -- a comment could stand in for a finding no reviewer ever wrote. Fixed by stripping HTML comments alongside fenced blocks before measuring. Added a fixture whose entire packet content is a single HTML comment and confirmed it still fails as thin. Verified the same way: reverted the fix, confirmed the fixture incorrectly passed (exit 0) on pre-fix code, restored the fix, confirmed it now correctly fails with onboarding_evidence.packet_too_thin. Re-ran the complete 665-fixture validator suite (all seventeen fixture modules) to confirm zero regressions from either change.

A thirteenth review round found the twelfth round's fence-stripping fix still recognized only triple-backtick fences, plus two unrelated real gaps. stripFencedBlocks() (check-onboarding-graph.ts) and the equivalent inline strip in check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts never stripped HTML comments or CommonMark's equally valid ~~~ tilde fence delimiter, so a required section, evidence-packet finding, or any other checked content relocated into either form stayed exactly as live and readable as before either file computed a fence-stripped view at all. Fixed both to strip <!-- ... -->, backtick fences of 3+, and tilde fences of 3+, in that order. Added requiredSectionInHtmlComment and requiredSectionInTildeFence (graph) and evidencePacketTildeFenceOnly (evidence packet) -- three fixtures, all confirmed to fail on the prior fix and pass on the corrected one via revert-and-restore. Second, ONB-17 (screen, control, and paywall contract) was domain.experience with no gate, the same verification-'none' gap already closed for ONB-03..09/19/20/21: an executor could return the declared artifact ID and fingerprint with no substantive contract behind it, and neither ONB-20's own gate nor the final graph gate ever read ONB-17-screen-control-paywall-contract.md. Fixed with the identical check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern -- gates: ['check:onboarding-evidence-onb-17'], wired into both package.json layouts and audit-plan.ts's exclusion list, with missing- and passing-packet fixtures. Third, ONB-22's own freshness gate cited the repo-wide check:generated-pages, which iterates every artifactPageEntries() entry -- so ONB-22 stayed verification-pending if any unrelated page (operations/orchestration.html, trust/security-review.html, ...) drifted, coupling this node's acceptance to lanes it does not own. Added a --page flag to check-generated-pages.ts that scopes assertions 2 and 3 (page exists, page matches a fresh render) to exactly one declared entry, skipping the repo-wide undeclared-page scan entirely in that mode; a new check:onboarding-page-fresh script (--page product/onboarding.html) replaces check:generated-pages in ONB-22's gates, while the unscoped script is untouched and still covers the general audit. Caught a real bug in this fix during its own verification: the first draft's --page flag definition omitted kind: 'string', so parseFlags() applied its default 'path' kind and silently resolved the value to an absolute filesystem path, breaking the manifest-key comparison entirely -- every scoped fixture failed even with the scoping logic itself correct. Fixed by adding the explicit kind, then re-verified: 5 new fixtures in repo-gates.fixtures.ts, including one proving the scoped check passes despite an unrelated page's drift while the unscoped check still catches that same drift, and one proving an unmatched --page value fails loudly (generated_pages.page_not_declared) rather than passing vacuously. Fourth, validation/repository/evals/launchbench/influencer-sponsorship-shortcuts.yaml's expected_guardrail and must_catch still prescribed a native review prompt 'after first value' -- the pre-onboarding-conversion.md doctrine that the round-7 knowledge-file sweep had already corrected everywhere else. Updated both fields to the canonical 'earn eligibility after real value and engagement, request outside first-run onboarding at a later natural success' wording from knowledge/experience/onboarding-conversion.md:94. Re-ran the complete validator suite (675 fixtures across all seventeen modules) to confirm zero regressions from any of the four fixes.

A fourteenth review round found eight more domain.experience nodes with no gate, the identical verification-'none' gap already closed for ONB-03..09/17/19/20/21 across rounds 6-13: ONB-10 (first-value and activation), ONB-11 (effort question audit), ONB-12 (state and identity contract), ONB-13 (analytics and experiments), ONB-14 (trust and lifecycle policy), ONB-15 (architecture decision), and ONB-16 (journey graph) each compiled to verification 'none' via compilePlan() -- an executor could return the declared artifact ID and fingerprint with no substantive packet behind it, and nothing downstream ever read the file even though ONB-15 fans in all five of ONB-10..14 and ONB-16/17/18/19/20 all depend on ONB-16 without reading it. ONB-18 (visual design prototype) had the same gap in a slightly different shape: its dependency on the Design Room state-mutate-version-render workflow proves the generic design flow ran, but proves nothing about whether this node's own packet is substantive. Fixed all eight with the identical check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern used for every prior node in this family -- gates: ['check:onboarding-evidence-onb-NN'], wired into both package.json layouts and audit-plan.ts's exclusion list (same rationale as check:onboarding-evidence-onb-03: each is the node's own catalog gate, and its output packet does not exist until a durable run produces it), with a missing-packet and a complete-packet fixture per node (16 fixtures total in onboarding.fixtures.ts). Did not re-verify the gate script itself via revert-and-restore, since check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts's fence-and-comment-stripping, thin-packet, placeholder-marker, and no-prose checks were already proven correct that way across rounds 12 and 13 for other nodes calling the same unmodified script -- verification here is check:catalog and check:gates-layout confirming every new gate resolves to a real npm script and every excluded script carries a rationale, plus the complete validator suite (691 fixtures across all seventeen modules: 690 passed, 1 expected pre-bump check:version-discipline failure) confirming zero regressions.

A fifteenth review round found the entry of the onboarding graph itself ungated, plus a genuine gap in how far the fence/comment-stripping fix reached. First, ONB-00 (resume and classify scope), ONB-01 (current-state trace), and ONB-02 (evidence plan) -- the three nodes that open the entire graph before ONB-03's evidence-research fan-out even begins -- were domain.experience with no gate, the same verification-'none' compile gap already closed for every other node in this family across rounds 6-14: an executor could return each node's declared artifact ID and fingerprint with no real scope classification, current-state trace, or evidence plan behind it, and ONB-03 would become runnable immediately with nothing downstream ever reading ONB-00/01/02's own packets, letting the entire graph and eventually the destructive ONB-22 cutover proceed without its foundational scope and evidence groundwork. Fixed with the identical check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern used for every prior node -- gates: ['check:onboarding-evidence-onb-00'/'-01'/'-02'], wired into both package.json layouts and audit-plan.ts's exclusion list, with a missing-packet and a complete-packet fixture per node (6 new fixtures). Second, and more consequential: the round-13 fence/comment-stripping fix in check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts and check-onboarding-graph.ts's stripFencedBlocks() paired every opening delimiter with a required closing one (/`{3,}[\s\S]*?`{3,}/g and its tilde/comment equivalents) -- so a packet or artifact that opened a backtick fence, tilde fence, or HTML comment and never closed it hit no match at all, and the regex stripped nothing. CommonMark still renders an unterminated fence or comment as extending to the end of the document (code or hidden, never prose), so this let a packet open one of these forms immediately, paste arbitrary unbounded text after it, and have that text still counted as live, substantive, prose content -- passing the 400-character length check and the hasProse check even though nothing after the unterminated opener actually renders as a real finding. Fixed by making the closing delimiter optional in both files via alternation with end-of-string (/`{3,}[\s\S]*?(?:`{3,}|$)/g and the equivalent tilde/comment forms), so an unterminated opener strips through the end of the text exactly as CommonMark would render it. Added a fixture per file -- an evidence packet whose only content sits inside an unterminated fence, and a required ONBOARDING.md section relocated past an unterminated fence opener -- both confirmed to fail on the prior (paired-delimiter-only) code and pass on the corrected one via full revert-and-restore: reverted both fixes, confirmed both new fixtures failed exactly as expected (2 failure(s) instead of 0), restored the fixes from backup, confirmed the diff matched the intended change exactly, and confirmed both fixtures passed again. Re-ran the complete validator suite (703 fixtures across all seventeen modules: 702 passed, 1 expected pre-bump check:version-discipline failure) and the full repo audit (61 ok / 2 expected-failed / 1 skipped pre-bump) to confirm zero regressions from either fix.

A sixteenth review round found the fifteenth round's own fix incomplete: its unterminated-fence regexes (/`{3,}[\s\S]*?(?:`{3,}|$)/g and the tilde/comment equivalents) treated ANY run of 3+ of the fence character as a valid closer, but CommonMark requires the closer to be at least as long as the opener -- a shorter same-character run inside an open fence is literal fence content, not a closer. A packet or artifact that opened a four-backtick fence, included a three-backtick decoy line, then placed real content and a genuine four-backtick closer after it, would have that content wrongly stripped to the decoy instead of the real closer, letting the content after the decoy (including the real closer line) count as live -- exactly inverted from the actual rendered result, where the whole span through the real closer stays hidden inside the still-open fence. Fixed by extracting a new shared stripNonRenderedMarkdown() helper into tooling/lib/launch-state.ts: a stripFenceChar() scanner tracks each opener's exact run length and only accepts a same-character closer of equal-or-greater length (falling through to end-of-string when none exists, preserving round 15's unterminated-fence behavior exactly), applied for both backtick and tilde delimiters after HTML comments are stripped. Both check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts and check-onboarding-graph.ts now import and call this one shared implementation instead of each carrying its own copy -- a deliberate deduplication, since the two files' copies had already drifted out of sync once before, between rounds 12 and 13, when one file's fence-stripping fix lagged behind the other's for an entire review round. Added two new fixtures (a required ONBOARDING.md section and an evidence packet, both placed past a too-short inner fence run that must not act as a closer) and verified via full revert-and-restore: reverted stripNonRenderedMarkdown to the old length-agnostic regex, confirmed both new fixtures failed exactly as expected (2 failure(s) instead of 0), restored the fix from backup, confirmed the diff matched the intended change exactly, confirmed both fixtures passed again. Re-ran the complete validator suite (705 fixtures across all seventeen modules: 704 passed, 1 expected pre-bump check:version-discipline failure) and the full repo audit (61 ok / 2 expected-failed / 1 skipped pre-bump) to confirm zero regressions.
